entries.title: pin the WebTransport H3_INVALID guard and fix http3 record counts
entries.body:
* fix(runtime): pin the WebTransport H3_INVALID guard and fix http3 record counts

net_webtransport_write_window calls WebTransport.write on a stream the
session does not hold, so a window outside its buffer answers H3_INVALID
from the WebTransport layer and the case fails once the guard is removed.
Http3Connection.readHeader's never-taken window guard now fails the
connection, as controlFrame's does, instead of returning a zero header.
The HTTP/3 record counts the slice and window sites the code has.

Tests: tests/link/net_webtransport_write_window

* docs(runtime): name only the HTTP/3 server's sends in the panic-site count
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: json-value bulk regrowth with one new Array, and the std/ audit for push-loop copies
entries.body:
jsonValueRoom and jsonValueRoomI32 now grow their buffer with one new Array and a guarded bulk set, replacing the per-element push loop that #2103 introduced. On the reported repro, parse cost drops below the 0.44.0 seed in both text and ranged modes. The std/ audit rewrote every other push-loop copy and fill to a guarded new Array plus a bulk copy, or recorded why it was left alone. The new lengths are proven non-negative rather than guarded by untested early returns. No panic site is added, and bench/instructions.json does not rise.

Verified: pr-adversary 3 rounds, CI green
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: declare the nish-cmp moves of the WebTransport H3_INVALID guard
entries.body: Declares the 10 nish-cmp pairs the WebTransport H3_INVALID guard moved against seed 0.50.0 (http3.ll in http-app, net_http_app, net_http_server_ws and net_tls_rsa_server), and drops the S8 relay declarations the 0.50.0 seed already ships.

entries.title: pin caller-proof exclusions for function values
entries.body: Pins the caller-contract cases the prover does not discharge for a function held as a value, with tests/link negatives and tests/cases positives, and aligns the NL2457 wording in src/panics.ts with docs/guide/errors.md.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: break-web builds without --allow-panics
entries.body: examples/break-web now builds under the no-panic default: its framebuffer keeps its fields private behind a Result factory, and the raster and random paths it reaches prove their indices or answer a Result, so the --allow-panics opt-out is gone.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: counted std rows that grow from empty after one new Array, and a check that every std module is counted
entries.body:
This adds six counted programs to the instruction gate. Each one grows a std structure from empty, so the bulk regrowth that #2449 rewrote with one new Array is now measured: std-json-value-parse, -reuse and -read, std-yaml-json-load, std-regex and std-text. Their baselines are CI's valgrind-3.26.0 counts.

The 19 existing rows that CI measured below their stored count are lowered to it. A new check compiles every counted program with its counted run's flags and fails when a scanned std module is reached by none of them and is missing from bench/instructions-exempt.txt. That file lists 42 modules, each with its reason.

Tests: tests/run.js instruction-coverage, instructions
Verified: pr-adversary 2 rounds, CI green
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: http-app builds without --allow-panics
entries.body: examples/http-app now builds under the no-panic default. The gzip reader checks its trailer through Crc32.ofRange and inflates through deflate's window-tested paths. Those paths answer an error code for a window outside the input, where the old reads panicked. The --allow-panics opt-out is gone, and the gzip instruction baseline is raised to cover the added checks.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: add crypto.tryGetRandomValues, an entropy builtin that answers instead of exiting
entries.body:
crypto.tryGetRandomValues(bytes) fills bytes from the OS entropy source like
crypto.getRandomValues, but answers false when the source fails instead of
exiting, so a program built under the no-panic default can turn the failure
into a Result. It is refused on wasm32, like its twin.
